reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen campus publishes 77 MW of IT capacity, second among Texas data centers, but its certifications point at regulated enterprise tenants rather than AI training.

The 77 MW is the second-largest single published figure in a state mapped to 133 data center sites, where capacity is published for fewer than one in seven. Texas totals 475 MW of published IT load, so that number is a floor on what exists, not a census. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this campus represents roughly 1,900 racks, spread across three co-located buildings, DFW3 through DFW5, totaling 976,000 square feet.

The certifications are the more telling detail. HIPAA, FISMA, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and SSAE 16 Type II qualify the campus for healthcare, federal, payment, and audited workloads. Those requirements shape who can lease the space and what they can do with it. Large-scale AI training carries no standard compliance requirement, so the compliance stack narrows the campus's addressability for that use rather than enabling it. Green Globes signals energy efficiency, which matters less when power is the binding constraint. The Dallas-Fort Worth metro has established power and fiber, but it is not among the largest AI cluster regions published to date.

What the data does not cover is whether any of this changes. No announced expansion is recorded, and the suitability score of 76 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type. There is no interconnection capacity, no power supply contract, no utilization figure, and no statement of intent to convert compliance-oriented space to compute. Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on decisions the specifications do not describe.
